note: The ground tiling immediately outside of the door to the northeast is off, and this is a recurring theme in the entryway of many buildings. When reading signs, it looks like there is supposed to be a second line, but instead it is attached without a space to the preceding line (as seen in the dialogue in white text on the screen) this large style sign does not look good. Use the smaller ones instead, always.

The tile blending for the riverbanks is off on this example of a bridge. Similar feedback was captured in the bridges section of the QA round. What's interesting is that the garden in the south part of the screenshot is actually significantly better than any of the gardens in the QA round. This garden is more or less perfect.
The riverbank tiling/borders have many small errors. They look like little fingers sticking out into the river with hard edges. This is pretty consistent throughout the level.

The player can walk on water. We already knew this, but it needs to be addressed. Additionally, the fish do not swim around. They are stationary until the player approaches very close. They should always swim around, regardless of how close the player is.
The room is too empty, with the entire southeast and southwest walls and the south corner being open and empty.
Good structure for an orchard, but too empty. Add a few crates of apples and some apples on the ground that the player can pick up.

The alignment on the cobblestone path is way off with the mausoleum and the gate. Similar feedback was given in the Q&A round. If the spacing, balance, and alignment were fixed, this would be excellent, though.
This shop needs much more object diversity. All it has is barrels. The shopkeeper behind the desk is good, though.

The crates of apples and the larger crate look out of place here. Move them up against the wall so they're out of the street. The female NPC is standing in an awkward spot, looking at the door in front of a door.

Two female NPCs clustered at the entrance of a door, one of them stuck in the frame of the door. The male NPC is also facing the door. He should be facing away from the building with his back to the wall. Another example of this very large sign that does not look right. use the smaller signs.
n/a
Most of the new items don't seem to actually have a function. They don't have a correct name or description. And their prices are not correct.

This town square is excellent. The benches are lined up in an organized fashion, and so are the lamp posts. Make all wells heal the player, as is the case in the nox campaign. To make it even better, add a second layer of cobblestone immediately around the well / center of the square.

The layout of this chapel is overall pretty good. It's just a little bit sparse and needs more pillars, benches, and statues. Also, it seems like the altar in this chapel is the only altar being used. Try some other objects as altars and chapels. Give the priest a better location instead of being behind a random pillar. Have the priest stand closer to the altar. This chapel is also better than any examples in the QA round.
Poor layout and organization, much like the examples in the QA round
Another example of tiling on the exterior of a door being wrong

Too much empty space. Similar to many of the QA around examples. the wall partition near the south corner suggests that that should be some sort of a nook or supply area, yet it's completely empty. The furnaces in the middle of the green carpet doesn't make any sense - place furnaces on a small brick square. Put a small brick hearth around the fireplace on the northeast wall.
The shopkeeper should be standing closer to the bar. The tiling underneath the bar is not blended with the tiling surrounding it.
The loaf of bread does not have a proper name or seem to do anything.
The northeast side of the carpet is clipped and not blended in with the surrounding floor. Center the bearskin rug in the room more. Add more bookshelves to the northwest wall.
The brick hearth around the stove is not properly bordered. Move the stove out from the corner a little bit. It's too far in the corner. The south corner of the room is way too empty.
